meta.title: AlmostThere — turn any goal into today's checklist
meta.description: AI breaks your goal down into monthly milestones, weekly targets and a concrete daily checklist. Rest and reflection included, pace adapts to how you actually do.

hero.title: You're almost there.
hero.subtitle: Tell us your goal and your deadline. AI breaks it down into monthly milestones, weekly targets and a daily checklist you can actually tick off — with rest and reflection built into the plan.
hero.ctaNote: The demo needs no account. See how your goal breaks down in under a minute.
hero.trustLine: For freelancers, founders, networkers, students — and anyone who wants a life with something to show for it.

how.title: One goal. Three levels. Today's list.
how.subtitle: The whole product lives or dies on the quality of this breakdown, so that's where we put the work.

steps.title: You set the goal and the date
steps.body: "Reach A2 in German by the end of the year." That's enough. Add your rest and reflection preferences and we take it from there.

steps.title: AI builds the skeleton
steps.body: Monthly milestones first — what has to be done by the end of each month for the deadline to hold. Then each month splits into weekly targets.

steps.title: You get today's checklist
steps.body: Concrete tasks for today, sized to the time you actually have. Rest days and reflection blocks are items on the list, not gaps between them.

features.title: What makes it different
features.subtitle: Not another task list. A planner that actually gets you there.

items.title: Top-down breakdown that holds up
items.body: Goal → months → weeks → days. Every level is derived from the one above it, so the daily task you tick off today provably moves the deadline closer.

items.title: Several goals, one honest day
items.body: Your day is a fixed budget shared by every goal you're chasing. AlmostThere schedules across all of them at once, so two goals never quietly demand the same evening.

items.title: Rest is part of the plan
items.body: Say you want one task-free day a week, or ten minutes of reflection daily — and the AI plans around it. Rest shows up as a checklist item, because a plan that ignores recovery is a plan you'll drop.

items.title: The pace adapts to you
items.body: We track how much you actually complete. Falling behind for a couple of weeks? You'll get the choice: slow the plan down and move the date, or catch up and carry on unchanged. Nothing is ever rescheduled behind your back.

items.title: Milestones you look forward to
items.body: Attach your own reward to each milestone — or let the AI suggest a few, sized to what you just pulled off. Something small for a weekly milestone; for the finish line, something you'll remember.

example.title: What a breakdown looks like
example.subtitle: Goal: reach A2 in German. Deadline: six months. One rest day a week, ten minutes of reflection daily.
months: Core vocabulary (greetings, numbers, days), pronunciation of the alphabet, the 100 most common words
Present tense of regular and irregular verbs, simple sentences about yourself
Everyday vocabulary (shops, restaurants, travel), asking questions
Past tense (Perfekt), longer conversations, listening to simple texts
Vocabulary expanded to A2 level, reading simple texts
Practice and prep for the exam or real conversation, full A2 recap
weeks: Alphabet, pronunciation, greetings and basic phrases
Numbers 1–100, days of the week, months
First 50 most common words + simple phrases
Another 50 words, recap the month, self-test

days.text: Go through the alphabet and its pronunciation (20 min)
10 minutes — write down what was hardest to remember today

pricing.limitsTitle: What ten plans a month means
pricing.limitsBody: A new plan counts when you create a goal. Everything after that — the breakdown into weeks and days, the daily tasks, replanning when your pace changes — does not count and is unlimited for a running goal. Ten new plans is room to try different wordings and deadlines; someone who sets a goal and works on it will not use half of it in a month. The app shows you how much is left.
